# Wire baseline fixtures

These baseline snapshots are independent of the session request encoder. They
were captured with bincode 2.0.1 standard serde encoding directly from the wire
declarations,
without `session`, `wire::request`, or the bounded encoder. Expected bytes are
checked in, never generated by the tests.

The release source is tag `0.21.0`; the source inspected when this PR was
created is
`78cbfff4fc963c81cebf24326090f7dcbdb4498d` (crate `0.22.0`). The relevant
`AgentInfo`/base/tail source is retained in `protocol-0.21.0-lib.txt`. Request-code
assignments from that tag are in `agent-request-codes.txt` and
`server-request-codes.txt`. These declarations and assignments are unchanged in
that inspected source, so both sets of binary snapshots are identical.
The protocol constants in both are `0.49.0` and `>=0.49.0`.

The session foundation now builds on `0.26.0`. The captured handshake and
response values remain unchanged. The request-code tests also pin the engine
commands (23–26) and reports (41–44) added in `0.23.0`; transport tests carry
`0.24.0` install requests with a selected privilege profile. These additions do
not change the historical snapshots.

The captured values are:

- Base handshake: agent name `agent`, agent version `1.2.3`, protocol version
  `0.49.0`, IPv4 address `127.0.0.1:8080`, status `Ready`.
- Complete handshake: that base, capabilities `node.package` and `registrar` in
  sorted order, active trust epoch `Some(42)`, manifest format range
  `Some({min: 1, max: 2})`, no provisioning fingerprint, no audit health.
- Power response: `Ok(NodePowerResponse::Initiated)`.
- Install preflight: `Ok(InstallPreflight::UnknownConfigTemplate {id: "custom"})`.
- Remote text: `Err("not supported")`, with unit success type.

Base bytes were encoded independently as a five-field tuple. Complete bytes used
the existing derived `AgentInfo::Serialize`. Responses used the existing typed
wire enums. The fixtures contain payload bytes only. Tests separately pin the
big-endian frame header, all little-endian fixed-width request codes, and standard
bincode integer bytes (`300_u32` is `fb 2c 01`, not a fixed-width body).

A tail ending before an entire optional field is valid; a present `Some` marker
without its value is malformed. Tests distinguish those cases and compare the
legacy and guarded decoders against these same fixtures.

## Framed handshake replies

The `handshake-acceptance.bin` and `handshake-rejection.bin` fixtures include
the four-byte big-endian frame length and the entire reply body. They were
captured by sending the pinned full agent handshake over loopback to
`server::handshake` from tag `0.21.0` (`76e28fe3`) and tag `0.27.0`
(`4b35f3e1`) before adapting the session handshake for the listener.
The capture used a requirement of `>=0.49.0` and a ceiling of `0.49.0`.
Acceptance used the fixture unchanged, and rejection changed the agent
version to `0.48.0`.

Both releases reply with `Ok("0.49.0")` on acceptance. The 0.21.0 rejection
contains only the requirement, `Err(">=0.49.0")`. The 0.27.0 release and
the listener report the full accepted range, `Err(">=0.49.0, <=0.49.0")`.
Both results use bincode 2 standard serde encoding. The listener replays
the acceptance bytes across all valid field boundaries and rejects
truncated present fields using the existing bounded decoder.

## Server processing in 0.27.0

The `current/server-*.bin` fixtures were captured against the released
0.27.0 source at `4b35f3e` before the typed server runners were added. They
include framing. Requests were composed from literal little-endian codes and
bincode 2.0.1 standard serde argument declarations. The legacy
`handle_authorized_with_context` emitted the captured response bytes over
loopback. Event bytes were composed from the legacy two-byte header and that
release's event codec, then checked through the legacy event stream helper.
Protocol 0.50.0 re-composed the frames whose payload types it replaced; see
below.

The request and response streams exercise all 32 built-in operations,
including default `not supported` responses, a handler refusal, and success
responses of several shapes. Certificate renewal includes ignored argument
bytes. After every handler result the dispatcher reads the next frame. Clean
EOF completes the stream. The fixture driver queues FIN after the legacy
dispatcher returns; the typed runner owns that step.

The denial fixture sends a second request on the same stream and pins the
`authorization denied` response followed by termination. The denial is
`PermissionDenied` with classification `Forbidden` in
the legacy API. A truly unknown numeric
code sends `unknown request code` and returns `InvalidData` with
classification `NotSupported`.
Each terminal fixture contains another request to verify dispatch stops.
The delegated fixture pins the call-site handoff with an opaque body and a
subsequent request. Complete malformed arguments return a local error with
no response. The legacy dispatcher classifies the argument errors for
`GetModel` and `GetOutliers` as `InvalidArgs`. Other parse errors retain their
original I/O error.

The event fixture has two ordered events, a complete undecodable frame in
between, and nonzero reserved header bytes. The truncated event fixture
shows the legacy helper invoking `on_stream_end` after a partial payload.
The truncated request fixture shows the legacy dispatcher returning clean
completion after a partial payload. Typed framing reports truncation as an
error to prevent incomplete messages from being counted as complete streams.
A truncated two-byte event header remains an unexpected EOF.

## Re-composed for protocol 0.50.0

Protocol 0.50.0 replaced the detection event payload (request 13 and the
event stream) and appended two fields to `DetectorStatusReport` (request
44). The frames carrying those payloads were re-composed the same way as
above, from literal codes and bincode 2.0.1 standard serde; every other
frame, including the undecodable and truncated ones, is byte-identical to the
0.27.0 capture.

- `server-requests.bin`, request 13: arguments `(1, 2, [event A])`, where
  event A is a `DetectionEvent` with time 0 (`00`), no sensor (`00`),
  detection model `LockyRansomware` (`02`), raw event kind `Conn` (`00`), no
  category (`00`), a `Subject` target (`01`) whose primary subject is
  `Cluster` (`01`) 0/1 (`00 01`) with no related IPs (`00`) and a window of
  0 to 0 (`00 00`), score `1.0` (`00 00 00 00 00 00 f0 3f`), and detail
  `LockyRansomware` (`02`). The handler still answers `not supported`, so
  the response is unchanged.
- `server-requests.bin`, request 44: the 0.27.0 arguments followed by empty
  `detection_models` and `excluded` (`00 00`). The response is unchanged.
- `server-events.bin`: the reserved header `ab cd`, event A, the complete
  undecodable frame `ff`, and event B, which is event A with cluster id 2
  and score `2.0` (`00 00 00 00 00 00 00 40`). The undecodable frame still
  fails on the leading `i128` time.

Requests 32 and 33 now answer `Vec<NetworkListItem>` instead of a
`HostNetworkGroup`, but their frames carry unit arguments and the fixture
handler answers them `not supported`, so neither their requests nor their
responses changed. The session runner replays the request stream for an agent
that advertised protocol 0.50.0: it answers these two pulls from an agent that
advertised an earlier version with its own error, without the handler.
